buku.title: A Beautiful Day
buku.creator: Raeesah Vawda, Lindy Pelzl, Elana Bregin
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: It’s a beautiful day for a picnic. Everyone wants to join in the fun.

halaman.alt: Mom and baby greet Nicholas as he stretches in bed.
teks: “What a beautiful day,” says Mom. “Wake up Nicholas.”
“Hello sun,” says Nicholas. “Good morning birds.”

halaman.alt: Dad and Nicholas sit at the breakfast table. Nicholas waves to his friend Jacob through the kitchen window.
teks: “It’s a lovely day,” says Dad. “Let’s have a picnic by the river.”
“Can my friend Jacob come?” asks Nicholas.

halaman.alt: The animals jump up and down with excitement. Nicholas and Jacob put their arms around each other.
teks: “Don’t forget me. I love picnics!” says Donkey.
“And me. I want to come too!” says Dog.
“Follow us,” say the birds.

halaman.alt: Dad carries a picnic basket on his head. Mom, the children and all the animals follow him to the picnic spot.
Nicholas and the dog get ready to race.
teks: “I’ll race you to that tree,” Nicholas says.

halaman.alt: At the tree, Nicholas bends over panting.
teks: “I won, I won,” says Donkey.
“Not fair,” says Nicholas. “You’ve got four legs.”

halaman.alt: Nicholas does a handstand. Jacob does a handstand on one hand.
teks: “Look what I can do,” says Nicholas.
“I bet you can’t do this,” says Jacob.

halaman.alt: Mom, Dad and baby arrive at the river bank.
teks: “Here’s our picnic spot,” says Dad.

halaman.alt: Nicholas, Jacob, Donkey and Dog leap into the river.
teks: “Race you to the water!” says Jacob.

halaman.alt: The family sits on a red and white checked picnic blanket and eat their snacks.
teks: “Come and eat, boys and girls,” says Mom.

halaman.alt: Outside Jacob's house, Nicholas waves goodbye to his friend.
teks: “Time to go home,” says Mom.“Say goodbye to Jacob.”

halaman.alt: Nicholas and Dog are fast asleep in bed, while Donkey sleeps outside under the stars.

buku.title: A Dancer’s Tale
buku.subtitle: The story of Phyllis Spira
buku.creator: Samantha Cutler, Thea Nicole De Klerk, Roberto Pita
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Phyllis Spira was dancing by the age of four. That was just the beginning of her journey towards becoming one of South Africa’s Prima Ballerinas.

halaman.alt: Phyllis's mom and dad cuddle their sweet baby girl. Everyone is smiling and happy.
teks: Once upon a time, not so far away, a baby called Phyllis was born for ballet.
Two people in love, her Mom and her Dad, could not have known yet what a dancer they had.

halaman.alt: Little Phyllis dances with two other young girls for their strict ballet teacher.
teks: When Phyllis was four she had us transfixed: impressing her teachers with ducky feet flicks.
Before school and after, she danced every day. Nothing pleased Phyllis more than ballet.

halaman.alt: Wearing a beautiful yellow dress, a teenage Phyllis twirls around a street sign in London. Big Ben is seen in the background.
teks: The world would soon see, when, only fifteen, she travelled to London to live out her dream.
Far from home and her friends, she was starting afresh. The Royal Ballet school would soon be impressed!

halaman.alt: Phyllis dances on points with a handsome male dancer.
teks: When she danced Swan Lake it was fit for the Queen! After years pirouetting, it was time to be seen!
She took to the stage, leaping, twirling about, with everyone smiling! They clap and they shout!

halaman.alt: Phyllis carries a suitcase and leaps across Earth. She wears a dress fringed with flags from around the world.
teks: From Mexico to Canada, the US to France, everyone asked her to visit and dance.
With the Royal Ballet, and all of her friends, she spread love for dancing so it never would end.

halaman.alt: Phyllis holds a South African flag in her arms. She wears an African-inspired dress and Table Mountain can be seen in the background.
teks: Still, Phyllis missed home, they’d been too long apart. She longed to return and to make a fresh start.
So she leaped and she bounded to her beautiful land, to walk once again on South African sand.

halaman.alt: Phyllis dances with a clock as the backdrop.
teks: Dance isn’t just fun, as Phyllis well knew: she worked day and night, and with hard work she grew.
Always smiling and tireless, through good times and tough,she aimed for her best.‘Good’ was never enough.

halaman.alt: In a beautiful blue costume, Phyllis dances on stage with a strong male dancer. The audience applauds appreciatively.
teks: Romeo and Juliet, Swan Lake and Giselle. She captured each audience under her spell.
With Gary Burne beside her, Eduard Greyling too, her dancing was magic in every review.

halaman.alt: With roses at her feet and a ribbon announcing her new title, Phyllis squeezes her hands with gratitude.
teks: Reward comes eventually, when you’re put to the test. And one day South Africa would call her the best:
‘Prima Ballerina Assoluta’, greatest dancer of all, her title forever.
Phyllis wanted no more.

halaman.alt: Phyllis gazes lovingly into her new husband's eyes as he swoops her into his arms for their wedding dance.
teks: Soon Phyllis found love when she met Philip Boyd, a dancer himself! They were both overjoyed.
In love, they soon married, and together they’d dance. No match could be better when given the chance!

halaman.alt: Phyllis corrects a small girl's arm position during a dance lesson. Two other children practise their steps.
teks: They didn’t have children but never were sad, for they had a way to help all moms and dads.
Their school, Dance For All, would give children a chance, from all walks of life, to learn and love dance.

halaman.alt: Phyllis looks out at the reader, while five other ballerinas dance on the page all around her.
teks: Her gift to the world and all her success help others to realise they can be their best.
They dance for us now, inspired by her feats,inspiring us, too, as we dream in our seats.

buku.title: A House for Mouse
buku.creator: Michele Fry, Amy Uzzell, Jennifer Jacobs
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Mouse is looking for a new house. Friendly animals offer to share their homes with him. But nothing is right until he finds his own little spot, warm and cosy.

halaman.alt: Mouse looks at a yellow house in the distance.
teks: Mouse was looking for a new house.

halaman.alt: The front door is ajar. Mouse looks inside.
teks: This looks like a nice house.

halaman.alt: A black puppy with a long tongue invites Mouse to join him.
teks: “You can come and sleep with me,” said Puppy.
“Thank you,” said Mouse.

halaman.alt: Mouse sleeps in a pool of mud.
teks: That night, Mouse’s dreams were bouncy and muddy.

halaman.alt: A colourful parrot on a perch invites Mouse to join him.
teks: “You can come and sleep with me,” said Parrot.
“Thank you,” said Mouse.

halaman.alt: Mouse sleeps in a wild forest.
teks: That night, Mouse’s dreams were noisy and wild.

halaman.alt: A goldfish swimming in a tank invites Mouse to join him.
teks: “You can come and sleep with me,” said Fish.
“Thank you,” said Mouse.

halaman.alt: Mouse sleeps underwater surrounded by fish and seaweed.
teks: That night, Mouse’s dreams were cold and wet.

halaman.alt: Mouse dashes past the skirting boards.
teks: Mouse needed somewhere warm and dry.

halaman.alt: Mouse perches on a couch in front of the fireplace.
A beautiful bookshelf.
teks: Mouse found a bookshelf nearby.

halaman.alt: Mouse sleeps peacefully.
teks: That night, Mouse had warm and cosy dreams.

buku.title: A Tiny Seed
buku.subtitle: The Story of Wangari Maathai
buku.creator: Nicola Rijsdijk, Maya Marshak, Karen Lilje
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: In a village on the slopes of Mount Kenya, a little girl worked in the fields with her mother. She worried as she saw the big forests disappearing, but she knew the power of a tiny seed.

halaman.alt: Wangari and her mother hold hands in a field.
teks: In a village on the slopes of Mount Kenya in East Africa, a little girl worked in the fields with her mother. Her name was Wangari.

halaman.alt: Wangari sows vegetable seeds into the earth.
teks: Wangari loved being outside. In her family’s food garden she broke up the soil with her machete. She pressed tiny seeds into the warm earth.

halaman.alt: It is twilight. Wangari carries her vegetables home.
teks: Her favourite time of day was just after sunset. When it got too dark to see the plants, Wangari knew it was time to go home.
She would follow the narrow paths through the fields, crossing rivers as she went.

halaman.alt: Wangari and her brother carry her bags to school.
teks: Wangari was a clever child and couldn’t wait to go to school. But her mother and father wanted her to stay and help them at home.
When she was seven years old, her big brother persuaded her parents to let her go to school.

halaman.alt: A copy book with drawings of the continents lies open on a table.
teks: She liked to learn!
Wangari learnt more and more with every book she read.
She did so well at school that she was invited to study in the United States of America.
Wangari was excited! She wanted to know more about the world.

halaman.alt: A magnifying glass is held over a yellow flower.
teks: At the American university Wangari learnt many new things. She studied plants and how they grow. And she remembered how she grew: playing games with her brothers in the shade of the trees in the beautiful Kenyan forests.

halaman.alt: Wangari sits on top of a pile of books and reads.
teks: The more she learnt, the more she realised that she loved the people of Kenya. She wanted them to be happy and free. The more she learnt, the more she remembered her African home.

halaman.alt: A single buck stands in a barren field.
teks: When she had finished her studies, she returned to Kenya. But her country had changed. Huge farms stretched across the land.
Women had no wood to make cooking fires. The people were poor and the children were hungry.

halaman.alt: Wangari shows an older woman how to plant in the earth.
teks: Wangari knew what to do. She taught the women how to plant trees from seeds.
The women sold the trees and used the money to look after their families.
The women were very happy. Wangari had helped them to feel powerful and strong.

halaman.alt: Small seedlings grow into fields of trees.
teks: As time passed, the new trees grew into forests, and the rivers started flowing again. Wangari’s message spread across Africa.
Today, millions of trees have grown from Wangari’s seeds.

halaman.alt: A portrait of Wangari wearing Kenyan headdress is surrounded by trees.
teks: Wangari had worked hard. People all over the world took notice, and gave her a famous prize. It is called the Nobel Peace Prize, and she was the first African woman ever to receive it.

halaman.alt: A beautiful old tree stands tall and proud in the field.
teks: Wangari died in 2011, but we can think of her every time we see a beautiful tree.

buku.title: Amazing Daisy
buku.creator: Nozizwe Herero, Siya Masuku, Leona Ingram
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: On a little farm lives Daisy, a little chicken who wishes she could fly. All the other chickens laugh at her daily flying practice. But one day something amazing happens …

halaman.alt: Daisy stands outside her chicken coop.
teks: Once upon a time on a little farm near a little village there lived a little chicken called Daisy.

halaman.alt: The other chickens laugh as Daisy tells them her plans.
teks: “When I grow up, I want to fly high, high into the sky,” Daisy said.
But all the other chickens laughed at her.

halaman.alt: The other chickens tease Daisy. Her mother comforts her.
teks: “You are so weird,” they said. “We won’t play with you anymore.”
“Daisy, we can all flap our wings but it’s very difficult for chickens to fly,” Mama told her.

halaman.alt: All alone, Daisy practises flying outside the chicken coop.
teks: Daisy wouldn’t give up.
Every day she practised by herself, flapping her wings.
Flap, flap, flap, she would flap her wings but she couldn’t lift off the ground.

halaman.alt: Daisy imagines herself flying.
teks: While she practised, she imagined herself flying high into the sky and looking at the chickens below.
She imagined herself flying past the sparrows and past the swallows.
“Wow!” the birds would say. “A chicken that can fly!”

halaman.alt: Daisy flaps her wings. Daisy crashes to the ground.
teks: So ... Flap, flap, flap, every day Daisy would flap her wings.
She would lift off the ground but fall down again.

halaman.alt: Daisy complains to her mother.
teks: “I’m never going to fly!” Daisy cried to Mama. “The others are right.”
“Daisy, you are different from the other chickens. They don’t want to fly but you do! You can do it,” Mama said.

halaman.alt: Daisy climbs the wall of the chicken coop.
teks: The following day Daisy climbed to the top of the chicken coop and flap, flap, flap, she flapped her wings.
She flew into the air and flapped her wings ...
and flapped her wings ...
and flapped her wings
and ...

halaman.alt: Daisy falls on the ground with a thud.
teks: BAM! The other chickens laughed out loud.“Ha ha ha! We told you! Chickens can’t fly!”

halaman.alt: Daisy flaps her wings and stays in the air.
teks: But the next day Daisy climbed even higher, right up to the top of the rondavel.
Flap, flap, flap, Daisy flapped her wings.
She flew into the air and flapped her wings ... and flapped her wings ... and flapped her wings and ...

halaman.alt: Daisy confidently flies alongside a swallow and a sparrow.
teks: She kept flying!
The wind beneath her wings grew stronger and she flew higher and higher!
The sparrows and the swallows said, “Amazing! A flying chicken!”

halaman.alt: The other chickens climb to the top of the chicken coop.
teks: And the other chickens wanted to be just like her.
They said, “Oh Daisy, you’re amazing!”

buku.title: Bathtub Safari
buku.creator: Tracy Lynn Chemaly, Robert McEwan, Sarah-Jane Williams
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Jack’s bath time takes a wild turn as things in his bathtub start to change, and a group of animals becomes part of his adventurous bathtub safari!

halaman.alt: Jack's mother pokes her head around the bathroom door. Jack relaxes in his bath.
teks: Bathtime is Jack’s favourite part of the day.
‘I’ll be back in a few moments,’ says his mom. ‘Make sure to clean behind your ears.’

halaman.alt: Jack sees something green and spiky move on the water.
teks: There’s a SWOOSH. And a swish of a tail.
And then...

halaman.alt: Jack gleefully rides on the back of a crocodile.
teks: Jack’s bathtub safari begins!

halaman.alt: Jack notices something twisting on the grey taps.
teks: Look at what’s coming!
There’s a twist and a turn..
Something’s growing...
It’s a...

halaman.alt: Jack stands on an elephant's back while it showers him with water.
teks: TOOOT!

halaman.alt: From the elephant's back, Jack notices something long and yellow.
teks: There’s a RUMBLE!
UP
UP
It’s going up
and...

halaman.alt: Jack swings from the neck of a giraffe.
teks: SPLASH!

halaman.alt: A sponge in the water turns into a hippopotamus.
teks: There’s a SPLOSH. Something bubbles.
It’s time to...

halaman.alt: Jack sunbathes on the hippo's back. From there he sees something orange.
teks: AAAAAAH
But something’s lurking in the background...

halaman.alt: A lion roars.
teks: ROAR

halaman.alt: Jack's mother is at the bathroom door. Jack lies alone in the bath.
teks: ‘Time to get out. I hope you’re clean and ready for bed.’

halaman.alt: Jack is fast asleep in bed surrounded by his toy animals.

buku.title: Come Back, Cat!
buku.creator: Nicola Rijsdijk, Karen Lilje, Sam Scarborough
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: A delightful tale about an independent cat.

halaman.alt: Cat hides under the couch.
teks: Come back, cat! Play with me.

halaman.alt: Cat leaps up and hangs off the curtains.
teks: Sit in your basket. Stay right here!

halaman.alt: Cat sits in her basket. She is grumpy.
teks: Come back, cat! That’s way too high.

halaman.alt: Cat sneaks out the back door.
teks: Come back, cat! Don’t go outside.

halaman.alt: Cat runs outside and chases butterflies.
Cat pulls a sock off the washline and unravels the thread.
teks: Come back, cat! That’s not yours.

halaman.alt: Cat finds a snail in the dirt. The sock thread is wound around her tail.
teks: Come back, cat! What have you got?

halaman.alt: Cat encounters a chicken. Cat now has thread around her tail and the snail on her back.
teks: Come back, cat.
That’s not your friend!

halaman.alt: Chicken feathers float around Cat's head. She still has the thread around her tail and the snail on her back.
teks: Hello, cat! Are you back?

halaman.alt: Cat lies in her basket looking satisfied.
teks: Stay in your basket. It’s nap time now.

halaman.alt: Cat's basket is empty except for a few feathers.
teks: Cat?

halaman.alt: Cat sleeps peacefully on the couch with the feathers, thread and snail.

buku.title: Graca's Dream
buku.subtitle: The STory of Graca Machel
buku.creator: Melissa Fagan, Karlien de Villiers, Marike le Roux
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: The inspiring story of Graça Machel, and her dream to instill a love for reading and learning in the children of Mozambique and the rest of Africa.

halaman.alt: Graça's mother is pregnant. With one hand on her belly, she gazes out at her barren village. A Mozambiquan flag droops from a pole in the distance.
teks: Graça was about to be born in a small village in Mozambique. The country was poor and the people did not yet rule themselves. Children didn’t have good schools and many couldn’t read. Graça’s mother dreamed of giving her children better opportunities. But without education there was little hope.

halaman.alt: Graça's pregnant mother and five siblings stand and cry by their father's sickbed. Their father dreams of his children reading.
teks: Baby Graça would be the sixth child. But with this joyous event there was great sadness. Their beloved father was dying. He dreamed that his youngest daughter would go to a good school. He knew that education would give her opportunities he never had. His family promised to make their dad’s dream come true.

halaman.alt: Little Graça sits on her mother's. Her mother reads a story.
teks: Just weeks after their dad died, the new baby was born. She was given a name to match the beauty and blessing that she was – Graça. As the years passed, Graça brought much joy to her family and they kept the promise made to their father. Graça would have a good education.

halaman.alt: Graça sits in the front row of a well-equipped classroom among white children. Her teacher stands before them.
teks: Graça worked hard at school and as a teenager she received a gift that would change her life. It was a scholarship to attend a rich city school.

She dreamed of becoming a teacher and using her education to educate others. She wanted the children of her beloved Mozambique to know reading and learning. She dreamed of a time when all children would go to school.

halaman.alt: A bespectacled Graça sits at a library desk surrounded by books.
teks: Graça did her best in that city school and years later she was blessed again. It was another scholarship to attend a university in faraway Portugal. She met new friends, learned new languages and read a bounty of books. She realised her dream of becoming a teacher.
All this made Graça very happy. There was only one thing that still made her sad...

halaman.alt: Graça stands under the shade of a tree teaching women and children from the village.
teks: Back at home people were still not free. But now Graça had an education, skills, and hope. She also had friends who felt as she did about children’s right to learn. She would use her knowledge and work with her friends. Together they would bring change to Mozambique.

halaman.alt: Happy citizens smile and wave Mozambiquan flags.
teks: Finally with the help of all her friends, Mozambique was free!

halaman.alt: Graça and Samora embrace on their wedding day. They dream of the house they will live in together.
teks: The man chosen to lead the country was Graça’s special friend, Samora Machel. They fell in love and got married.

halaman.alt: The children with no books look sad. The children who have books are happy and proud.
teks: Graça was given the important job of making sure that all children in Mozambique got a good education. It was a hard job because there were so many children in Mozambique who couldn’t read. She knew that they needed education and wanted to make real change in her country. She started with primary schools and getting boys and girls into classrooms. Literacy was her focus and putting books into children’s hands.

halaman.alt: Graça and Samora read to their two young children on the couch. In the distance a plane explodes on the tarmac.
teks: Graça and Samora had two children. They shared a dream to create good lives for their own family and for the Mozambican people. They were happy and hopeful.
Then one terrible day, Samora died in an aeroplane crash.

halaman.alt: An older Graça and Nelson Mandela stand in the field with a group of happy children.
teks: Graça mourned Samora for many years, but she found love again. She met a man who had also spent his life dreaming of bringing freedom, hope and education to his people.
Graça married Nelson Mandela and together they worked to help Africa’s children.

halaman.alt: Graça hands out books to the children of her village. Children can be seen reading everywhere.
teks: Here’s a book, my child. What will it inspire you to do?

buku.title: Grandpa's Gold
buku.creator: Kerry Saadien-Raad, Elsabé Milandri, Mathilde de Blois
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: The children are talking about their grandpas. Giraffe’s grandpa can build a skyscraper. Elephant’s grandpa can cook a massive feast. But whose grandpa will give the children the biggest surprise?

halaman.alt: Elephant, Giraffe, Mountain Goat, Cheetah and Monkey are discussing their grandpas.
teks: The children were talking about their Grandpas.

halaman.alt: Grandpa Giraffe builds a tower of bricks that touches the clouds.
teks: My Grandpa can build a tower to the sky, said Giraffe.
Once he built a skyscraper for a king.

halaman.alt: Grandpa Cheetah holds a fishing rod. He stands next to a whale in a bath.
teks: My Grandpa can fish for anything in the sea, said Cheetah.
Once he caught a whale and kept it in his bath.

halaman.alt: Grandpa Mountain Goat proudly stands at the peak of a mountain.
teks: My Grandpa can climb to the clouds in the sky, said Mountain Goat.
He climbed the tallest mountain in the world, in just four hours.

halaman.alt: Grandpa Elephant wears a chef's cap. He holds a plate of jelly, a whisk, a tea towel and a tower of cakes. Colourful balloons float all around him.
teks: My Grandpa can cook a feast, said Elephant.
Once he cooked a meal for a president’s birthday party. All by himself.

halaman.alt: Monkey points to his teeth and tells his friends about his Grandpa.
teks: Well my Grandpa doesn’t build or fish or climb or cook, said Monkey. But he owns gold!
He hides it in his mouth. And at night he soaks it in a glass of water.

halaman.alt: The animals fight.
teks: No, he doesn’t! Yes, he does! No, he doesn’t!
Well, come and see if you don’t believe me, said Monkey.

halaman.alt: The children follow Monkey to go and find his Grandpa.
teks: So the children went to see Monkey’s Grandpa.

halaman.alt: Monkey's Grandpa sits in an armchair. Some of his teeth are gold.
teks: You see? said Monkey. And he can take them out.

halaman.alt: The childen crowd around Grandpa Monkey.
teks: No, he can’t! cried the animals.

halaman.alt: Grandpa, tongue hanging out his mouth, holds his false teeth up in the air.
teks: Waaah! said Grandpa Monkey. And there are enough ...

halaman.alt: The children all smile... with gold teeth in their mouths.
teks: ... for everyone!

buku.title: Hippo Wants to Dance
buku.creator: Megan Andrews, Sam Beckbessinger, Marisa Steyn
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Hippo wants to dance. Won’t anyone dance with her?

halaman.alt: Hippo stamps her big feet on the ground. Dust clouds appear.
teks: Hippo wants to dance.
She jumps up and down on the dusty ground.
THUMP! THUMP!

halaman.alt: Shongololo is curled up at Hippo's feet. He shakes his finger disapprovingly.
teks: “You’re getting dirt on me!” says Shongololo, sleeping in the sand.
“Go dance somewhere else.”

halaman.alt: Hippo splashes in the river among the bulrushes.
teks: Hippo wants to dance.
She rolls into the river and splashes her arms and legs.
SPLISH! SPLASH!

halaman.alt: Kingfisher perches on a branch and shakes water off her feathers.
teks: “You’re making me wet!” says Kingfisher, hunting for her breakfast.
“Go dance somewhere else.”

halaman.alt: Hippo stands on the ground and kicks her fat legs in the air.
teks: Hippo wants to dance.
She twirls around and around in a field, kicking her legs up high.
SWOOSH! SWOOSH!

halaman.alt: Three Meerkat babies enjoy a bubble bath. Meerkat sticks his nose in the air and waves Hippo away.
teks: “Be careful! You nearly kicked me!” says Meerkat, bathing his babies.
“Go dance somewhere else.”

halaman.alt: Hippo happily flops down in a puddle of mud.
teks: Hippo wants to dance.
She flops into a puddle of mud and slides around on her nice big belly.
SQUISH! SQUASH!

halaman.alt: Donkey carries buckets of water on his back. They wobble and splash everywhere.
teks: “Why don’t you stop dancing?” asks Donkey, carrying his buckets.
“Why can’t you do something useful instead?”

halaman.alt: Hippo sits down dejectedly. Grasshopper stands nearby.
teks: Hippo is sad.
She is too sad to dance.
She sits on a rock and cries. The tears roll down her cheeks and fall on the ground.

halaman.alt: As Hippo's tears fall, Grasshopper dances.
teks: HOP! HOP!
Grasshopper hears Hippo’s tears.
He starts dancing around her feet.
PLOP! PLOP!

halaman.alt: Hippo and Grasshopper dance together. Hippo is happy again.
teks: Hippo and Grasshopper start to dance, and the other animals come to look ...

halaman.alt: All the animals dance together.

buku.title: How About You?
buku.creator: Renate van Rensburg, Margot Bertelsmann, Ronèll Botes
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: You don’t need to be alike to be friends. When two very different children meet an unusual creature, it’s a chance to ask, How About You?

halaman.alt: A girl wearing dungarees and a cap and a boy wearing a tutu and playing a guitar stand in a puddle.
teks: Who are you?

halaman.alt: A monster dripping goo looks in their direction.
teks: Is that goo?
Eeuw!
I want some too.

halaman.alt: A block with the number 2 stands in the puddle. The number 632 is written in goo.
teks: We are two.
How old are you?
Six hundred and thirty two?

halaman.alt: The girl wears blue. The boy wears red shoes.
teks: I like blue. Do you too?
I choose two shoes.
Which do you choose?

halaman.alt: The monster has horseshoes for eyes.
teks: Horseshoes!?

halaman.alt: A ball, a toy car and some marbles lie in a puddle.
teks: I make toys with boys.

halaman.alt: The boy and the monster shout.
teks: We make lots of noise.
Whaaa!
eurgghhh...aargh!

halaman.alt: The girl sleeps on a woman's back.
teks: I take a nap on Gogo’s back.

halaman.alt: The boy sits in the puddle, wide awake.
teks: I don’t nap!

halaman.alt: The moon and the sun shine.
teks: I stay upright all through the night.

halaman.alt: Someone kicks a ball into the monster's goo.
teks: The ball goes THWOCK! Buddy, you ROCK!

halaman.alt: The monster and the children hold hands.
teks: That’s what we do. How about you?

buku.title: Hugs in the City
buku.creator: Kalynne Vorster, JP Brouard, Milly Buys
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction

buku.title: I Can Dress Myself
buku.creator: Nontobeko Kunene, Heidel Dedekind, Bridget Krone
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction

buku.title: I Will Help You
buku.creator: Fathima Kathrada, Olivia Villet, Andrea Abbott
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: When Mama Heron needs help, Lungile comes to her rescue.

halaman.alt: Mama Heron is tangled in barbed wire in the river. Her chicks are far away in their nest.
teks: “Ouch!” Mama Heron hurts her wing and leg on barbed wire.

halaman.alt: A taxi drives past the river. It doesn't stop. Mama Heron calls out to a bus, which also doesn't stop. A boy cycles past but doesn't stop either.
teks: “I am hurt. I can’t get home to my children.”
“Please help me.”

halaman.alt: Lungile walks along the river bank with his push car. He asks Mama Heron why she is crying.
teks: “Why are you crying Mama Heron?”
“I can’t get home to my children.”

halaman.alt: Lungile pushes Mama Heron  in his push car.
teks: “I will help you,” says Lungile.

halaman.alt: Lungile kneels beside the car and talks to Mama Heron.
teks: “Thank you, Lungile!”

halaman.alt: Gogo hands Lungile some coins. Afterwards he swims in the river with his friends.
teks: The next day, Gogo sends Lungile to the shop to buy bread.
On the way, he stops to play with his friends in the river.

halaman.alt: Lungile stands with his friends and turns out his pockets. They are empty. He walks away. He is very sad.
teks: Eish! The money is gone.

halaman.alt: Gogo is cross! She has her hand on her hip and she shouts at Lungile.
teks: “Don’t come home until you find that money!”

halaman.alt: Lungile sits on the river bank and cries. Mama Heron flies towards him.
teks: “Why are you crying, Lungile?”

halaman.alt: Still crying, Lungile tells Mama Heron what has happened.
teks: “I lost the money Gogo gave me to buy bread. We have no supper now.”
“I will help you.”

halaman.alt: Mama Heron looks into the water. Lungile is excited.
teks: Mama Heron’s sharp eyes see the coins shining in the water.

halaman.alt: Lungile hugs Mama Heron.
teks: “Thank you, Mama Heron.”

buku.title: Is There Anyone Like Me?
buku.creator: Fred Strydom, Jess Jardim-Wedepohl, Stephen Wallace
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: I wonder if there’s another me somewhere in the world…

halaman.alt: Donkey lies on the grass and wonders to herself.
teks: I wonder if there’s another me somewhere in the world.

halaman.alt: She leans over the river bank and gazes at herself in the water. She brays loudly across the cliffs.
teks: Who looks the same.
And talks the same.

halaman.alt: Donkey stands next to Hippo and Mouse and they compare their curly tails.
teks: And even has my curls.

halaman.alt: Donkey looks up at her pointy ears with her big green eyes. Donkey laughs.
teks: Someone with my eyes my ears.
Who even has my laugh.

halaman.alt: Donkey and Hyena jump over the rocks.
teks: Who can do what I can do ...

halaman.alt: Monkey peels a banana. Donkey and Guinea Fowl look at the banana. They are confused.
teks: ... and can’t do what I can’t.

halaman.alt: Donkey is at the park. She peers around a tree.
teks: I’ve looked and looked everywhere to find another me.
I went down to the park and looked behind the trees.

halaman.alt: Donkey looks closely at Bird in her nest and Mouse in his hole.
teks: I looked around, up and down ...

halaman.alt: Donkey examines Buffalo, Giraffe and Elephant across the watering hole.
teks: ... at every single face.

halaman.alt: Donkey looks at her own shadow.
teks: I couldn’t find another me in any single place.

halaman.alt: Donkey smiles and all the other animals smile too.
teks: There’s only one me in the world!
I’m special, oh it’s true!

halaman.alt: Donkey winks.
teks: But not just me, don’t you see?
There’s only one of you!

buku.title: It Wasn't Me
buku.creator: Alexandria Mackinnon, Gwendoline van der Merwe, Lesley Beake
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction

buku.title: Karabo's Question
buku.creator: Leisl Jobson, Natalie Propa, Marike Beyleveld
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Little Karabo watches all the grown-ups in her family, and wonders, ‘What do I do? What do I know?’

halaman.alt: Kifue runs after a rooster.
teks: My sister Kifue chases roosters that crow.
What do I do?
What do I know?

halaman.alt: Katleho throws a ball in the yard.
teks: My brother Katleho has a ball to throw.
What do I do?
What do I know?

halaman.alt: A boy kneels on the ground. He holds a trowel.
teks: My cousin Kutloano plants seeds in a row.
What do I do?
What do I know?

halaman.alt: A girl stands on one leg and leans on her hoe.
teks: My cousin Kamohelo leans on her hoe.
What do I do?
What do I know?

halaman.alt: An old woman sits outside a hut and sews.
teks: My aunt Keromang has a dress to sew.
What do I do?
What do I know?

halaman.alt: A man walks with a cow. He holds a stick.
teks: My uncle Khotso herds the cattle that low.
What do I do?
What do I know?

halaman.alt: Mama dries wheat on the ground.
teks: Mama dries wheat when the wind does not blow.
What do I do?
What do I know?

halaman.alt: Papa rides his horse.
teks: Papa rides a horse over mountains in snow.
What do I do?
What do I know?

halaman.alt: Grandpa smokes a pipe and walks with his donkey.
teks: Grandpa’s slow donkey walks to and fro.
What do I do?
What do I know?

halaman.alt: Grandma sits by a fire and sings.
teks: Grandma sings songs till the fire burns low.
What do I do?
What do I know?

halaman.alt: A small child looks confused.
teks: You know how to say yes.
You know how to say no.
That’s what you do!
That’s what you know!

halaman.alt: The small child dances. The rest of the family clap their hands!
teks: Everyone laughs when you put on a show.
Your work is to play.
Your work is to grow.

buku.title: Katiiti's Song
buku.creator: Kirsten Walker, Maya Marshak, Philippa Namutebi Kabali-Kagwa
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction

buku.title: Lara the Yellow Ladybird
buku.creator: Martha Evans, Catherine Holtzhausen, Nadene Kriel
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: A yellow bug in a world of red, Lara the Ladybird just wants to fit in.

halaman.alt: Lara sits on a flower. She watches the other ladybirds. They all have red wings. Her's are yellow.
teks: Lara the ladybird was a special bug.
Unlike all her friends, she had bright yellow wings.

halaman.alt: Lara's mother sends her off to school. On her way she waves to Manto Mantis and Bibi Butterfly.
teks: Everyone loved her yellow wings.
Each morning, Bibi Butterfly said hello.
And Manto Mantis always waved.

halaman.alt: Sesa Spider hangs from her nest. Lara arrives at school. Her friends are happy to see her.
teks: Even Sesa, the sulky spider, was happy to see her.
At school, she played with lots of friends.

halaman.alt: At home, Lara cries to her mother. She dreams of red wings.
teks: But Lara wanted to be like the other ladybirds.
“I wish I had red wings like you, Mama,” she cried.

halaman.alt: Lara stands on a chair in front of the mirror. Her mother paints are yellow wings using a tin of red paint.
teks: So one day, to cheer her up, Lara’s mother painted her wings bright red.

halaman.alt: On the way to school, Lara waves to the other insects. They don't wave back.
teks: The next morning, nobody greeted Lara on her way to school.

halaman.alt: Lara arrives at school. Her friends don't greet her.
teks: And when she got there, none of her friends said hello.

halaman.alt: Lara sits alone. She cries to her teacher.
teks: Lara sat all alone. No one noticed her new red wings.
Until Miss Miya spotted her and said: “You’ve painted your lovely yellow wings!”

halaman.alt: Miss Miya tells the children what Lara has done. They are shocked.
teks: Lara’s classmates were shocked.
“Your wings are special!”
“So unique!”“So rare!”

halaman.alt: Miss Miya tells Lara about Sipho's large spot and Sally's long legs.
teks: “Lara,” Miss Miya said, “your yellow wings are what make you you.
Like Sipho’s spot ... and Sally’s legs.”

halaman.alt: Lara lies in the bath and scrubs the red paint off her wings. Her wings are yellow again.
teks: Back home, Lara took a long bath and scrubbed until her golden wings gleamed.
“I’ll never paint my wings again!” she thought.
Except, maybe once or twice ...

halaman.alt: Lara holds a paintbrush. Her wings are painted with colourful dots and stars and stripes.
teks: To try a bit of purple ... or something nice.
But not for ever and just for fun.

buku.title: Little Ant's Big Plan
buku.creator: Candice Dingwall, Steven McKimmie and Telri Stoop
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: This is a story about a little ant with a big plan, and how his love for reading saved the day.

halaman.alt: Little Ant wears glasses and sits on top of a book. The other ants hold items of food.
teks: Little Ant loved to read. Little Ant was often teased.
“Ants don’t read. Ants must feed. Ants collect the food they need.”

halaman.alt: A boy lies on a picnic blanket reading a book. The ants carry away his picnic food.
teks: Little Ant would read all day, he’d read and read the day away.
The other ants took what they found to store for winter underground.

halaman.alt: Inside his ant heap, Little Ant's Mum and Dad scold him about reading books all the time. His little sister watches with interest.
teks: His mum and dad got really mad, and Little Ant felt really bad.

halaman.alt: The trees are bare and autum leaves are all around. The ants look under the leaves and collect a discarded apple core.
teks: In autumn when the leaves fall down, the ants must keep food underground.

halaman.alt: The Queen addresses the ants.
teks: The Queen wants food to fill the store, so all the ants must work some more.

halaman.alt: Little Ant's thought bubble shows a hamburger and a restaurant table.
teks: Little Ant begins to shout about a place he read about.
“A restaurant is what we need, a place where people go to feed.
It says so in the books I read.”

halaman.alt: The ants march through the day and into the night.
teks: The ants go marching one by one.
They march into the setting sun.

halaman.alt: Little Ant reaches a burger restaurant with tables inside and out.
teks: And Little Ant said “Hey, there’s one!”

halaman.alt: The ants carry hot dogs, burgers and chicken drumsticks through the day and into the night.
teks: The ants go marching one by one, carrying a burger, carrying a bun.

halaman.alt: The Queen shakes Little Ant's hand. The rest of the ants cheer.
teks: When they return the Queen is glad.
The stores are full. They cheer like mad.

halaman.alt: Inside his ant heap, Little Ant's Mum and Dad hug Little Ant. His little sister beams happily.
teks: Ant gets hugs from mum and dad.

halaman.alt: The boy is reading a book. Little Ant and his little sister hold hands on top of the boy's shoulder.
teks: His baby sister takes his hand “Now I think I understand.”
“The way you love to read a book ... Makes me want to take a look.”

buku.title: Little Sock and the Tiny Creatures
buku.creator: Lili Probart, Jon Keevy, Chani Coetzee
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: It’s wash day for the Socks, but where has Little Sock gone?

halaman.alt: Little Sock is in the laundry basket with the other socks.
teks: It’s wash day for the Socks.

halaman.alt: Little Sock falls out the basket. He falls far away from the other socks.
teks: OH NO! Little Sock falls out!
“I have to get home,” says Little Sock.

halaman.alt: Little Sock asks the toys how to get home.
teks: “Do you know the way home?” asks Little Sock.

halaman.alt: Robot hands him a cracker. Little Sock drives off in the toy car with the cracker on the back seat.
teks: “No, but take this,” says the Robot.

halaman.alt: Little Sock pokes his head into a mouse hole. Mouse is at his table playing Poker.
teks: “Do you know the way home?” asks Little Sock.

halaman.alt: Mouse hands Little Sock a cracker.
teks: “No, but take this,” says the Mouse.

halaman.alt: Outide Mouse's house, Little Sock meets a spider. Its web is filled with buttons.
teks: “Do you know the way home?” asks Little Sock.

halaman.alt: Spider hands Little Sock a blue marble from a collection by his web. The marble rolls away.
teks: "No, but take... OOPS!!!”

halaman.alt: The marble continues to roll away.
teks: “Maybe the marble knows the way home,” says Little Sock.

halaman.alt: The marble stops rolling by a chest of drawers.
teks: “It does!” says Little Sock.

halaman.alt: Little Sock sits in the drawer with the other socks.
teks: Little Sock is happy.
Different socks have different personalities, so pick your favourite.
MAKE YOUR OWN LITTLE SOCK
YOU WILL NEED:
• a sock
• two buttons
• a needle and thread
• a grown-up to help
INSTRUCTIONS
Ask your grown-up to sew the buttons onto the sock.

buku.title: Londi the dreaming girl
buku.creator: Lauren Holliday, Nathalie Koenig
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Londi loves to dream all day. But where will her dreams take her?

halaman.alt: Londi stands on the grass looking up at the clouds.
teks: Londi was a dreaming girl. Up in the sky, she didn’t see clouds.

halaman.alt: The clouds are shaped like geese and fish and sheep.
teks: Instead Londi saw flying geese, jumping fish, and fluffy sheep running home.

halaman.alt: Londi lies on the grass. Gogo comes outside.
teks: One afternoon, Gogo came outside, looking tired.
“Londi, stop dreaming!” she said. “It’s time to go and fetch the water.”

halaman.alt: Londi's feet are on the grass.
teks: Londi stood up and smiled at her feet.
“Let’s go, feet! You know the way there!”

halaman.alt: Londi walks to the tap carrying her bucket.
teks: Londi started walking to the tap. She hopped over the rocks.
She crept past Mama Neli’s house. She dashed down the path.

halaman.alt: Londi stands behind others in the queue for the tap.
teks: The line at the tap was long. “Oh no!” Londi said to her feet.
“We’ll have to wait. Let’s stay in line. No dreaming away!”

halaman.alt: There is a shiny purple shoe in the bush.
teks: Ooh! Londi thought. But what’s that shining over there?
I wonder who lost their shoe?

halaman.alt: Londi dreams of a girl wearing only one purple shoe. She also dreams of a pig wearing three purple shoes.
teks: Did it belong to a girl like me?
Or something else...

halaman.alt: Londi crouches down next to a yellow bird and her chicks.
teks: And what’s that under there?
Cheep! Cheep!

halaman.alt: Gogo stands with her hands on her hips. She has a big shadow.
teks: And what’s that big shadow? Uh oh, it’s Gogo!
“Londi, your bucket nearly rolled away!”
“Sorry, Gogo. I dreamed too far, again.”

halaman.alt: The setting sun smiles. Londi watches. Gogo carries the bucket home.
teks: They filled up the bucket together. Londi watched the big sun sink into the hills.
“Come let’s go, my dreaming girl,” said Gogo.

halaman.alt: Londi looks up and sees a pink pig in the sky.
teks: “Look, Gogo! There’s a pink pig in the sky!”
“Oh Londi... It’s just a cloud,” Gogo sighed.
Londi took Gogo’s hand and they walked home together happily.

buku.title: Lory Dory
buku.creator: Sonia Dearling, Brendan O'Neill, Arthur Attwell
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Lory Dory was born invisible. No one understands that she is real. Until, one day, she finds a way to show them who she is.

halaman.alt: A little girl lies in bed. Her grandpa sits next to her.
teks: One night Grandpa was tucking me in.
His hands were soft and his hair was thin.

halaman.alt: Grandpa talks to the girl.
teks: ‘I’m going to tell you a special story, about a girl named Lory Dory.’

halaman.alt: There is an empty armchair. Two eyes peek out. This is Lory Dory.
teks: You couldn’t see Lory Dory at all because she was born invisible.

halaman.alt: The falling rain makes an outline of Lory Dory. There is an outline of Lory Dory underneath the blankets on a bed.
teks: You’d only see Lory when rain hit her head, or when she was curled under blankets in bed.

halaman.alt: Children are playing in the snow and pointing at the outline of Lory Dory made by the snow.
teks: Lory was left out of all the kids’ games. They teased her and they called her names.
‘Look, it’s Lory. The Imaginary Friend! She’s not like us, she’s just pretend!’

halaman.alt: A boy sits at his school desk. Lory Dory sits next to him and draws.
teks: One day at school, a boy wanted to know:
‘How do you look? I only see you in snow.’

halaman.alt: The boy hands Lory Dory a paint brush.
teks: ‘Can you paint yourself?’ Lory knew that she could.
But not in the same way the boy thought she would.

halaman.alt: The picture is filled with paintings of cats and fruit and stars.
teks: Lory painted her body with all that she loved from the world all around and the sky up above.

halaman.alt: The paint makes footprints on the page.
teks: She painted herself every day with such pride, to bring out the person who she was inside.

halaman.alt: There is a painting of Lory Dory standing by the trees wearing a beautiful dress and smiling happily.
teks: I know I’m invisible and hard to see.
So I painted these pictures to show the real me.’

halaman.alt: Grandpa stands by the little girl's bed.
teks: ‘Are you making this up, Gramps? Is this story true?’
‘Lory is real – real as me, real as you.’

halaman.alt: The little girl lies in bed alone. Coloured light twinkles through the open door.
teks: When Grandpa had left me, I can’t quite be sure, but I think I saw Lory just outside my door.

buku.title: Maddy Moona's Menagerie
buku.creator: Rachel Zadok, Candace Di Talamo, Nick Mulgrew
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: It’s Maddy Moona’s birthday and she really wants a pet! But which silly animal will picky Maddy get?

halaman.alt: Maddy Moona is dressed in black and white. She wears a party hat.
teks: My name is Maddy Moona, and today I’m turning five.
Dad promised I could choose a pet, a real one! Something live!
We’ll travel across the whole wide world, searching Mali through Tibet, until we find the perfect one...
Oh, I know just what I’ll get!

halaman.alt: Maddy rides on an elephant's back. Her party hat lifts off her head with the force of the elephant's sneeze.
teks: I’m going to get an elephant. I’ll ride on it to school.
My brother Billy can walk behind, he’ll think I’m awfully cool.
But... what if Ellie caught a cold? I guess she’d sneeze.... A LOT!
There is no tissue big enough to wipe up all that snot.

halaman.alt: A giant crocodile lies in the bath. Maddy helps him floss his teeth.
teks: I want a Nile crocodile sent to me by the pharaohs.
I’ll call him Tut and feed him soup, fish fingers, and baby marrows.
I’ll keep him in the bathtub and brush his pearly whites,
But... what if flossing all those teeth takes me all day and night?

halaman.alt: Maddy stands against the wall of a sweet shop. Two porcupines wearing balaclavas shoot quills at her.
teks: Perhaps a pair of porcupines, for games of robbers and cops.
Their prickly quills will be handy for holding up sweetie shops.
I can munch away on candy bars while my gang sharpen their spines.
But... what if my sharp-shooting pals put me in the firing line?

halaman.alt: In the sweet shop, Maddy stands in the foreground holding her nose. In the background a skunk lets off nasty smells.
teks: Maybe I need a stealthier plan. Let’s clear out the store with funk!
There isn’t a smellier critter on earth. That’s what I want — a skunk!
But... what if I can’t go into the shop after Skunky has let off his stink?
Sweets are no good for my teeth anyway. A rotten idea! I need to rethink!

halaman.alt: Maddy rides on a rhino's neck. It blows steam out of its nose and chases her baby brother, Billy.
teks: A rhino! The horns, the big stomping feet, the armour on both of its flanks!
Billy would never chase me again. It would be my own personal tank.
But... what if Billy raises his temper and Rhino goes on the rampage?
Crash bang boom! The teacups! The plates! Now I’m grounded ‘til I’m gran’s age.

halaman.alt: Maddy holds a piece of steak out to a lion curled up on the ground. Billy's dummy hangs from its mouth.
teks: I need a beast to tame my brother. With teeth, sharp claws and a roar.
A LION! I could feed it Billy biltong... Yes! A lion would settle the score.
But... a lion has a huge appetite. Skinny Billy won’t satisfy.
And once Brutus has a taste for us Moonas, he’ll see me as Maddy stir-fry.

halaman.alt: A python wraps itself tightly around Maddy's whole body and blows kisses.
teks: Dad thinks I should choose a cuddlier pet. My parents are so hard to please.
They want me to have a pet I can hug. A python?
A python has squeeze.
But... if Snakey develops too much of a crush, he’ll suffocate me with affection.
To be honest, I just can’t marry a snake! And reptiles can’t handle rejection.

halaman.alt: Maddy sits on a chair with a giraffe. The ceiling of the room lifts off above the giraffe's curled neck.
teks: No, reptiles aren’t the way to go. I definitely need something taller.
A giraffe would be awesome. I’ll slide down her neck, and think up a long name to call her.
But... something more than eight foot tall is no good. Our house has a rather low ceiling.
I’d spend hours massaging cricks out her neck. My fingers would lose all their feeling.

halaman.alt: Maddy stands alone. She shrugs.
teks: None of these are the perfect pet!
Oh what, oh what will I get?

halaman.alt: Maddy sits on the ground. A black and white puppy plays next to her with a red ball.
teks: Those animals just don’t work. None are my perfect partner in crime.
I want something with fur, a pet who will follow.
Oh wait! I know — a canine!

halaman.alt: Maddy lifts the puppy in a happy hug.
teks: My Bandit is the biggest bark on the block! He’s the fastest pup in the west!
Nothing can stop us. Not Billy nor bedtime. I love my Bandit.
He’s my best!

buku.title: Miss Helen's Magical World
buku.subtitle: The Story of Helen Martins
buku.creator: Jacqui L'Ange, Wendy Morison, Nadene Kriel
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: This is the story of Helen Martins’ battle against darkness, told by one of the creatures she loved best, the wise old owl.

halaman.alt: An owl introduces Helen and her house in Nieu Bethesda.
teks: Meet my friend Helen. She was born in a little Karoo town called Nieu Bethesda. There was not much going on in this town. But she made a whole world here. She even made me. And she named her house after me.
It was called ‘The Owl House’.

halaman.alt: A young Helen wears men's clothes and has a carboard box on her head. The other girls wear dresses and look at her with disgust.
teks: Most of Helen’s nine brothers and sisters were grown up and gone by the time she arrived. But she still had her sisters Annie and Alida.
Helen didn’t have many friends in the village, but she didn’t mind.
From the start, Helen did things differently from most people.

halaman.alt: Helen reads a postcard. It has pictures of camels and princes and pyramids.
teks: After her sisters left home, Helen lived alone with her parents. She loved her mother, but she hated her father. Everyone agreed he was a very strange man.
Her big sister Alida travelled all over the world. One day she sent Helen a postcard from Egypt.
In her mind Helen saw princes and pyramids and camels in the sand.

halaman.alt: Helen reads a poetry book. She reads the line: "Ah moon of my delight who knowst no wane..."
teks: As she grew older, Helen read more stories of faraway places. She especially liked poems from Persia in the Middle East.
She dreamed of visiting the ocean one day. She kept a seashell on her bedside table, and imagined she could hear the sound of waves inside it.
But of course, owls were always her favourite things of all!

halaman.alt: Helen leaves her classroom with a man. She is carrying a suitcase with clothes hanging out of it.
teks: Helen loved books and stories so much that she decided to become a teacher. She was very good at it too. But then she met Johannes Pienaar. He was also a teacher, and a writer and actor.
He convinced her to run away with him.

halaman.alt: Helen returns home with her suitcase.
teks: Helen and Johannes got married. They travelled to many different towns, teaching and performing plays. Helen thought she might start a family like her sisters had done. But it was not to be. She and her husband were always fighting.
When Helen’s mother became very sick, she decided it was time to go back home.

halaman.alt: Helen holds up a burning candle.
teks: Helen was not happy. Her mother was so sick, and her father was so grumpy. She kept to herself. People thought she was strange.
The night her mother died, Helen kept a candle burning beside her bed all night.
With the help of that little light, Helen didn’t feel so afraid of the dark.

halaman.alt: One of Helen's helpers creates an owl sculpture in her garden. There is a sign in the background which reads: "This is my world."
teks: Helen decided she wanted brightness in her life. She began by changing the space around her.
She needed helpers. Three men from the village, Jonas Adams, Piet van der Merwe, and Koos Malgas, made the things she imagined out of wire and cement.
She filled her back garden with interesting creatures. There were sphinxes and camels, mermaids and cats. And lots and lots of owls! She called it her camel yard. On the fence she made a wire sign.
It said: ‘This is my world’.

halaman.alt: Helen sleeps by the light of the many lanterns she has created.
teks: During the day Helen made sculptures. At night, she practised catching light.
She collected glasses and mirrors, candles and lamps. Anything that would shine.
She put lanterns in every room. Mirrors caught and reflected the light. She covered the walls in glittering glass so that they could shine too.
After Helen’s father died, she had the house to herself. Each night she slept in a different room.
She would always choose the one with the best view of the moon and the stars.

halaman.alt: Helen stands amongst her sculptures in the garden. She is smiling and holding a cup of tea. The owl sits on her shoulder.
teks: The people of Nieu Bethesda would walk past Helen’s garden and marvel at the creatures in it.
Some of the village children brought her glass bottles for her sculptures and called her ‘Miss Helen’. She always thanked them with sweets.
Others were not so friendly. They called her names and threw stones on her roof.
Miss Helen spent all her money on glass and cement. She lived on bread and black tea.
In her diary she wrote: “In my loneliness I am happy.”

halaman.alt: Helen is an old woman. She sits in her house with the garden sculptures visible through the window.
teks: The garden grew and grew, until there was hardly space left for any more creatures.
Miss Helen was tired now. Her hands were stiff and sore. Her eyes were going blind from working with tiny bits of glass.
She wasn’t afraid of being alone. But she was still afraid of the dark. And her world was getting darker and darker. She knew that soon she wouldn’t be able to see anything at all.

halaman.alt: Helen flies into the sky with the owl.
teks: But when she closed her eyes for the last time, Miss Helen didn’t see darkness. She saw the sun and the moon and the stars. She saw wise men and mermaids, camels and cats, acrobats and owls with big brown glittering glass eyes.
And we still stand here today, just the way she left us, in the garden she made, looking East.

buku.title: Mrs Penguin's Perfect Palace
buku.creator: Helen Brain Faulkner, Vian Oelofsen, Jennifer Jacobs, Celeste Beckerling
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: The Penguin family lives on the beach, surrounded by rubbish. Until one day, Mrs Penguin says: we need a house! But how will they build one?

halaman.alt: Mrs Penguin and Papa Penguin talk.
teks: “I wish I had a HOUSE!” said Mrs Penguin. “I don’t like living in rubbish.”
“Dear Mrs Penguin,” said Papa Penguin. “We will build you a palace.”

halaman.alt: Sissie Penguin scratches herself. Boetie Penguin holds a measuring tape. Gobbles wears a nappy. Mrs Penguin works.
teks: So the Penguin family set to work.
“The sand is making me itch,” grumbled Sissie.
“The measurements are wrong,” said Boetie.
“I’m hungry,” said Gobbles.
Mrs Penguin sighed. She was doing all the work.

halaman.alt: They have built a sandcastle. The sea washes it away. The Penguin family is sad.
teks: At last the castle was finished.
But the tide came in and washed it away.
“We’ll try again,” said Papa Penguin.

halaman.alt: The Penguin family carry stones with their flippers. They also use a wheelbarrow.
teks: “Come children, we’ll build Mama a mansion from stone.”
So the Penguin family set to work.

halaman.alt: Sissie holds a tower of stones; Boetie gets tangled up with his measuring tape. Gobbles shakes his rattle and cries.
teks: “The stones are heavy,” grumbled Sissie.
“The measurements are wrong,” said Boetie.
“I’m still hungry,” said Gobbles.

halaman.alt: They have built a stone house. The wind blows it down. Mrs Penguin shouts!
teks: At last it was finished.
But the wind came up and blew it over.
Mrs Penguin was cross.
“I’m not doing any more work,” she said.

halaman.alt: Papa Penguin talks to Boetie and Sissie. Mrs Penguin holds Gobbles.
teks: “We’ll try again,” said Papa.“I can’t think of anything,” said Sisi. “It’s too hard.”
“We haven’t got any cement,” said Boetie. “You can’t build a proper house without cement.”
“I’m hungry,” said Gobbles.
Mrs Penguin sighed. She was never going to get her home.

halaman.alt: Mrs Penguin points at all the rubbish on the beach.
teks: “Just look at all this mess,” she said.
Then Mrs Penguin had an idea.

halaman.alt: Boetie carries a pile of wood; Sissie drags a fishing net. Gobbles pulls a toy trolley filled with plastic. Papa brings Mrs Penguin a hammer.
teks: “Boetie, fetch wood,” she said.
“Sissie, find nets.”
“Gobbles, pick up plastic.
Papa, fetch the hammer.”
All day they worked.

halaman.alt: Sissie cries. Boetie is tangled up in his measuring tape. Mama works. Gobbles has a tantrum on the beach.
teks: I’m tired,” said Sissie.
“Keep working,” said Mama.
“The measurements are wrong,” said Boetie.
“Keep working,” said Mama.
“I’m still hungry,” said Gobbles.
“Keep working,” said Mama.

halaman.alt: Mama and Papa talk. The family works hard.
teks: “It’s going to be wonderful,” said Papa.
“You’re doing a good job,” said Mama.
So they worked and worked and worked and worked...
...and at last the house was finished.

halaman.alt: The house is finished. It is made from all the rubbish found on the beach. The whole family is happy.
teks: “Welcome to your palace,” said Papa. Mrs Penguin clapped her flippers. “Thank you,” she said. “It’s Mrs Penguin’s Perfect Palace.

buku.title: Queen of Soweto
buku.subtitle: The Story of Basetsana Kumalo
buku.creator: Jessica Taylor, Mia du Plessis, Marli Fourie
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Basetsana Kumalo is a beauty queen, but she’s also so much more. She teaches us that true beauty is about having a heart filled with love and generosity. Her story shows us that if you have courage and determination, you can achieve your dreams – whatever they may be.

halaman.alt: A young Basetsana stands with her family.
teks: Basetsana Makgalemele was born in a township called Soweto. She was her parents’ third daughter. They named her Basetsana, which means “girls”. In Tswana culture, calling your daughter that means your next child will be a boy. This actually happened. Her parents’ next child was a boy. Her parents, big sisters and younger brother all called her Bassie for short.

halaman.alt: Bassie stands alone while the other children look away.
teks: When she was a child, Bassie was very shy. She liked to sing and dance in her room on her own.
One day at school netball practice, the coach told two girls to pick teams. Bassie stood on the edge of the field hoping someone would say, “Come play with us!” But nobody wanted her on their team.
Little did they know, Bassie would become one of the most popular girls in the country.

halaman.alt: Bassie and her siblings sell sandwiches at a soccer match.
teks: On weekends, she and her brother and sisters helped their teacher mom and bus driver dad to pay the bills. They made sandwiches to sell at local soccer matches. They tried to sell everything as fast as they could so they had time to play with the other children when the game was over.

halaman.alt: Bassie looks at her reflection in a mirror.
teks: By the time Bassie turned 16, she was a beautiful young woman. She was so beautiful that she won two beauty competitions in one year: Miss Soweto and Miss Black South Africa.
But Bassie was not only beautiful on the outside. She was also beautiful on the inside. Even though she was a beauty queen, she still cared about the community where she grew up.

halaman.alt: Bassie stands in a science classroom in her school uniform. She wears a head girl badge.
teks: Bassie was also very smart. She worked hard at school, especially on her favourite subject: science. Her hard work was rewarded when she was the top science student at her school in matric. That’s not all, she was also Head Girl. The shy little girl was now one of the most popular girls in school.

halaman.alt: She is crowned Miss South Africa.
teks: Bassie’s father always encouraged his children to read. He gave her a book called The Power of Positive Thinking. From that book, she learnt that being optimistic is the key to making your dreams a reality. She dreamt of winning Miss South Africa. Not only did that dream come true, she was even crowned First Princess in the Miss World competition!

halaman.alt: Young Bassie holds her mother's hand. Then, as a young woman, she appears on TV.
teks: Bassie’s mother was her role model. Bassie described her mom as a “fierce, hardworking Xhosa woman who did not suffer fools”. She was a teacher and Bassie had plans to follow in her footsteps, but things don’t always go as planned! After winning Miss South Africa, she became a TV presenter. She wasn’t a teacher, but like her mom, she was hardworking. Her career in TV led to her opening her own television production company. She was now a successful business woman.

halaman.alt: Bassie holds a baby and talks to a group of children.
teks: Bassie’s motto is: “To whom much is given, much is expected.” She believes that you are given a gift so that you can give to others. Bassie does this by volunteering, giving of her time and money and even creating jobs. She is involved with projects and charities to help people in her community. One that is very close to her heart is the Nelson Mandela Institute.

halaman.alt: She stands next to Nelson Mandela.
teks: Bassie had a very close relationship with Nelson Mandela. When she was crowned Miss South Africa, Madiba wrote her a letter of congratulations. In the letter, he called her “our Queen”. They shared a passion for children and education and the belief that an educated nation can help fight poverty.

halaman.alt: Bassie holds Romeo's Kumalo's hand.
teks: In 2002, Bassie married Romeo Kumalo and became known as Basetsana Kumalo.
Together they established the Romeo & Basetsana Kumalo Family Foundation. The foundation looks after orphans - children who don’t have a mom and dad.

halaman.alt: Computers, phones, family and notebooks whirl around Bassie - she has to balance all these things.
teks: Bassie has had to learn to balance her busy work and family life.

She has her own company called Basetsana Women Investment Holdings. She and Romeo have three children, two boys and a girl. Bassie sees her role as mother to her children as her “highest calling and greatest privilege”.

halaman.alt: Bassie looks at her reflection in the mirror.
teks: Bassie says the secret to her success is “courage, determination, passion and staying committed to the course”. Despite all her success, she remains humble while trying to make the world a better place.
Being beautiful on the outside is not what makes you a beautiful person. It’s a heart filled with love and generosity. And that’s why Bassie is our beautiful Queen.

buku.title: Rafiki's Style
buku.creator: Louis Greenberg, Audrey Anderson, Wesley Thompson
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Rafiki’s style is all his own, but when the Cool Cat Crew struts by, he starts to wonder if it’s good enough.

halaman.alt: Rafiki watches soccer on TV with his aunt and uncle. The soccer player wears a red and yellow soccer shirt. His hair is stripey like a zebra.
teks: On Sunday, Jimmy Zogba scored the winning goal.

halaman.alt: Rafiki wears his usual white shirt. The Cool Cat Crew wear red and yellow soccer shirts and zebra hairstyles.
teks: On Monday, the Cool Cat Crew strutted by.

halaman.alt: One of the Cool Cat Crew points to his zebra hair. Rafiki looks glum.
teks: “Hey, Rafiki, where’s your zebra hair? Your hair’s so plain, like you don’t care.”

halaman.alt: Another member of the Cool Cat Crew shows Rafiki the fake tatoo of a soccer ball on his arm.
teks: “Hey, Rafiki, where’s your fake tattoo? Your skin’s so boring. You are too.”

halaman.alt: The third member of the gang points to his gold teeth. Rafiki touches his own teeth.
teks: “Hey, Rafiki, where’s your bling? Your teeth are wonky, that’s the thing.”

halaman.alt: Rafiki walks on the pavement, head hung low.
teks: That day, Rafiki walked home slowly.

halaman.alt: Rafiki's aunt prepares to cut his hair.
teks: “Auntie, can I have zebra hair?”
“I can’t cut you zebra hair. Actually, I wouldn’t dare.”

halaman.alt: Rafiki's sister sits and draws. Rafiki asks her to draw him a tattoo.
teks: “My skin’s so boring, Sisi. Can you make a fake tattoo?”
“You don’t need one to look like you.”

halaman.alt: Rafiki talks to his uncle while his uncle fixes a car.
teks: “Mkhulu, I wish I had some bling.”“Bling, my child, don’t mean a thing.”

halaman.alt: Rafiki watches soccer on TV with his aunt and uncle. The soccer player wears a white shirt and his hair is shaved like Rafiki's.
teks: The next weekend, Santi Ramires scored the winning goal.

halaman.alt: Rafiki wears his usual white shirt. The Cool Cat Crew wear white soccer shirts. Their hair is now shaved.
teks: On Monday, the Cool Cat Crew strutted by.
“Hey, Rafiki! Looking fine!”

halaman.alt: Rafiki stands with his aunt and uncle and sister. He shrugs.
teks: Rafiki shrugged. “I look like me; this style is mine.”

buku.title: Sbu's Special Shoes
buku.creator: Mark Hardie, Eidin Griffin, Megan Pirie
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Sbu’s little brother finds Sbu’s favourite shoes. When he tries them on, he discovers something very special about them.

halaman.alt: Sbu tries on a pair of big red takkies. A chicken sits next to him.
teks: These are my big brother Sbu’s shoes.

halaman.alt: Sbu runs with the shoes on. The chicken watches.
teks: Look what I can do in them.

halaman.alt: Sbu sprints with his push car. The chicken flies above him.
teks: I can race cars!

halaman.alt: The dog chases Sbu. The chicken flies above.
teks: Sometimes, I even race our bouncy dog.

halaman.alt: Sbu is number one! The chicken stands next to him.
teks: With Sbu’s shoes I win every time.

halaman.alt: Sbu and the chicken put their hand out - wait!
teks: Wait!
Let me show you one more thing.

halaman.alt: Sbu and the chicken dance.
teks: Watch me dance and spin.

halaman.alt: Sbu and the chicken do cartwheels.
teks: I can cartwheel over and over.

halaman.alt: Sbu hangs upside down from a tree branch. The chicken watches.
teks: I’m a monkey! Look at me hang upside down.

halaman.alt: Sbu leaps over the houses. The chicken watches from a roof.
teks: Watch me jump and catch the moon.

halaman.alt: Sbu holds the shoes in his hands.
teks: Here, try them on!

halaman.alt: The chicken tries the shoes on!
teks: See what you can do in Sbu’s special shoes.

buku.title: Searching for the Spirit of Spring
buku.creator: Mosa Mahlaba, Selina Morulane, Sibusiso Mkhwanazi
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Nkanyezi can’t wait for the Spring festival, but the people of Ndlovu have lost their spirit of celebration. She must go in search of the spirit of Spring. What will she find?

halaman.alt: Young Nkanyezi holds a butterfly in her hand. She looks out over her village.
teks: The Winter cold had passed.
Spring was coming to Nkanyezi’s village. Soon the villagers would gather to celebrate the new season. Nkanyezi looked forward to the Spring festival more than any other day in the year.

halaman.alt: Nkanyezi stands outside a hut. She looks worried. Two women talk inside.
teks: One warm morning, Nkanyezi overheard two village elders talking about the festival.
“The people of Ndlovu have lost their spirit of celebration,” one sighed.
“How can we have a Spring festival in a village that has forgotten how to celebrate?” asked another.

halaman.alt: Nkanyezi has an idea.
teks: Nkanyezi was worried.
“How will the sun shine again unless we sing to wake it from its winter slumber?” she asked herself.
Nkanyezi thought for a long time.
“I must find what we have lost,” she decided.
“I must go in search of things that will bring backthe spirit of celebration to my village.”

halaman.alt: Three women give Nkanyezi a bag. They send her on her way.
teks: The elders gave Nkanyezi their blessing for the journey. They gave her a bag to carry the things she would find.
Nkanyezi was afraid, but she believed she would succeed.

halaman.alt: Nkanyezi sails alone in a boat.
teks: Nkanyezi walked all day. She hiked up a hill, and down into a valley. She sailed across the great river, and climbed between sharp rocks. She marched across the plains until she reached the shadow of the red mountains.

halaman.alt: A kind woman holds a bottle of yellow paint.
teks: As night was closing in, Nkanyezi arrived at a village of patterns and colours as she had never seen before. She told the village elders about her journey to bring back the spirit of celebration to her people
The mother of this tribe gave Nkanyezi a gift.She told the girl, “With love we give to you this paint to restore colour to a village that has gone dull.”
Nkanyezi thanked the elders and put the paint in her bag.
Early the next morning she went on her way again, excited with this gift of colour.

halaman.alt: Nkanyezi walks through a forest of trees.
teks: Nkanyezi walked all day, through a vast forest of giant trees. As the sky became too dark for her to see, she heard the sound of beating drums. She hurried towards the drumming, feeling the spirit of dance coming to her tired feet.

halaman.alt: Nkanyezi stands behind a tree. She watches a tribe dance around a fire.
teks: Nkanyezi found herself in the village of the Bhubezi. People were sitting around a fire, drumming and singing. She had never before heard such wonderful music.
She told the village elders about her journey to bring back the spirit of celebration to her people. The Bhubezi invited her to rest and stay the night.

halaman.alt: A royal woman hands Nkanyezi a drum.
teks: In the morning the chief called on Nkanyezi.
“My child,” he said, “here is a special drum. It plays a new song every time you beat it.”
Nkanyezi thanked the elders and put the drum in her bag. She went on her way again, delighted with this gift of music and dance.

halaman.alt: Nkanyezi smells something on the breeze. She smiles.
teks: On the third day of her journey, as she a passed a field of fat cows, her nose started to tingle. An aroma tickled her taste buds and her mouth started to water. She followed the scent, and arrived in a village to find people standing over steaming pots of stew.

This tribe was famous for its feasts and Nkanyezi had never before tasted such flavours. After she had eaten her fill, she told the village elders about her journey to bring back the spirit of celebration to her people.

halaman.alt: Three women hand Nkanyezi a jar of spices.
teks: The next day, the council of cooks gave her a secret spice blend.
“Our daughter,” they said, “with these spices, happy tummies are guaranteed! We give you the gift of good food.”
Nkanyezi thanked the elders and put the spices in her bag.
She knew she had everything she needed. With new energy she started the long journey back to the village of Ndlovu.

halaman.alt: Nkanyezi leads all the villagers in a parade. They play music and sing. She throws glitter in the air.
teks: When she arrived home the villagers gathered around her to hear of her adventures. She told them the tales of what she had seen, heard, and eaten. Then she opened her bag to share the gifts given. The people rejoiced to receive these treasures.

Through the generosity of others and the courage of Nkanyezi, the villagers again found the colour, song and dance in their lives. And so the spirit of celebration was restored to the village of Ndlovu.

buku.title: Shongololo's Shoes
buku.creator: Marteli Kleyn, Megan Lotter, Jacqui L'Ange
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Shongololo has lost his shoes, and the other animals are NOT being very helpful. Will he ever find them?

halaman.alt: Shongololo only sees four of his yellow gumboots on the floor.
teks: Where are all my shoes?
I know I left them here!

halaman.alt: It is raining and Hedgehog holds up an umbrella made from one of Shongololo's yellow gumboots.
teks: I haven’t seen your shoes.
Go ask Snail!

halaman.alt: Snail sits on top of a mushroom. His new shell is a bright yellow gumboot!
teks: No shoes here.
Go ask Giraffe.

halaman.alt: Giraffe rides a bright pink bicycle. He uses one of Shongololo's shoes as a helmet.
teks: I’m in a hurry – go ask Frog.

halaman.alt: Frog floats down the river in one of Shongololo's shoes.
teks: Shoes? How many?
Go ask Flamingo.

halaman.alt: Flamingo dances in a puddle. She wears two of Shongololo's shoes as earrings.
teks: Seen your shoes?
No, not me.

halaman.alt: Shongololo lies down in despair and starts to cry.
teks: Will I ever find my shoes?

halaman.alt: Fox stands under a tree drinking tea out of a yellow shoe.
teks: Shoes, eh? You should ask the Monkeys

halaman.alt: The monkeys are in the tree. They play tin can telephone with two of Shongololo's shoes.
teks: We’re busy. Go ask Owl, she knows everything!
Hello hello?

halaman.alt: Owl sits on a branch and reads a book. There is a yellow gumboot filled with pens and pencils next to her.
teks: Hmm. I have an idea. Why don’t you ask Lion?

halaman.alt: Lion preens himself in front of the mirror. His mane is arranged in tight curls held in place by nine of Shongololo's gumboots.
teks: These are yours? I’ll give them all back if you come to my party!

halaman.alt: All of the animals enjoy a party under the stars. Shongololo finally wears all of his shoes.

buku.title: Sima and Siza
buku.creator: Lwando Xaso, CClaire Ingram
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Sima wants to be a nurse one day. His favourite game is hospital-hospital. But papa and his friends do not approve. What will change their minds?

halaman.alt: A boy has a tea party with his doll. The rest of the toys watch.
teks: Simamkele loves dolls. Mama buys him lots. They keep his loneliness away. Sima’s favourite doll is Siza. Sima wants to be a nurse when he grows up.

halaman.alt: Sima puts Mama's white skirt around his neck. Siza watches.
teks: He loves to put on Mama’s skirt, and twirl. Like magic, he suddenly becomes Sima the nurse. He plays hospital-hospital and makes sickly Siza and all his dolls better.

halaman.alt: Sima takes Siza to school. The other children point and whisper.
teks: Wherever Sima is, Siza is there too.

halaman.alt: A boy sticks Siza in the toilet. Sima watches with horror.
teks: But Sima’s friends do not like Siza. One day, they took him away and stuck his head in the toilet.

halaman.alt: Sima plays with Siza on the step. Papa stands over them with his hand on his hip.
teks: When Papa came home, Sima was nursing Siza.
‘What are you doing?’ asked Papa.
‘I’m being a nurse,’ said Sima. ‘Will you play with me?’
‘Yes. But we will go to the park and play soccer,’ said Papa.

halaman.alt: Papa, Sima and his friends play soccer.
teks: His friends saw Sima and Papa playing soccer. They joined in. Sima and Papa often play soccer now. But they still haven’t played with dolls.

halaman.alt: Sima wears his nurse outfit. He runs to the house.
teks: One day, Sima was playing hospital-hospital with his dolls. He heard Mama shout. ‘Sima! Run! Papa is waiting to play with you at the park.’

halaman.alt: Papa shouts at Sima. A tennis ball flies through the air.
teks: ‘Why on earth are you wearing a dress?’ said Papa in an angry voice. Just then a ball flew out of nowhere and ...

halaman.alt: Papa sits on the ground. He is injured. Sima's blanket is tied around his head.
teks: ... knocked Papa down. Everyone panicked. Except Sima. He knelt and tied his blanket around Papa’s bleeding head.
‘Call an ambulance!’ he shouted.

halaman.alt: A male nurse loads Papa into the ambulance. He talks to Sima.
teks: ‘He needs stitches in his head. You did just the right thing,’ said the nurse. Sima was proud.

halaman.alt: Sima and the male nurse high-five each other.
teks: ‘You’re a hero. You’ll make a great doctor one day.’ ‘But I want to be a nurse, just like you,’ said Sima.

halaman.alt: Papa joins Sima and Siza's tea party.
teks: ‘Thank you, Nurse Sima,’ said Papa.
Now Sima and Papa play hospital-hospital and soccer – and his friends do too.

buku.title: Sindi and the Moon
buku.creator: Thokozani Mkhize, Wesley van Eeden, Zanele Dlamini
buku.subject: Juvenile Fiction
buku.description: Sindi buzzes with colourful songs and dance. Will starting school end all that?

halaman.alt: Sindi sits on the ground and feeds the chickens.
teks: Sindi was a very lively little girl who loved to sing and dance. She lived on a farm with her parents and her Gogo.
Sindi enjoyed following Gogo around and feeding the animals.

halaman.alt: Sindi is excited. She dreams of pens and pencils and books.
teks: One evening while Sindi and her family were having dinner, Sindi’s mother had something to tell her. “Sindi,” she said, “after the long Christmas holidays, you are going to go to school.
”Sindi was so excited. She was happy that she would finally get to learn how to read and write.

halaman.alt: Sindi hops and skips.
teks: When Sindi was happy, she danced. Her joy spread to the farm animals. The dogs barked more loudly. The cows mooed more beautifully. The butterflies flapped their wings and landed in her hair.

halaman.alt: Sindi dances in the field.
teks: When Sindi danced, she swayed from left to right, as if she were pushed and pulled by the wind. She sang along with its soft, slow music.

halaman.alt: Sindi asks Gogo about school.
teks: As the holidays were ending after Christmas, Sindi started to wonder what school would really be like. She did not want her mother to know that she was nervous, so she asked Gogo what school would be like.
“School is very serious,” Gogo said. “There is no more time for song and dance, only learning.” This did not make Sindi happy at all.

halaman.alt: Sindi sits outside under the stars.
teks: The night before school started was very hot. Sindi just could not sleep! She tiptoed outside and sat on the stoep, looking up at the dark sky. The moon was big and bright and beautiful and the stars were twinkling.

halaman.alt: Sindi talks to the moon.
teks: Sindi spoke to the beautiful moon. “Dear moon so bright,” she said, “are you afraid of the dark? Is that why you ask the stars to keep you company?”
“I am going to school tomorrow, what will it be like?”
“Will they let me sing? Will they let me dance?”

halaman.alt: The moon smiles. The stars dance.
teks: Sindi started to sing. What she saw next made her rub her eyes in disbelief. Was she dreaming? The moon was smiling! And the stars were dancing to her song!
